title: Postmortem: SEV-2 Serving runtime KV-cache eviction storm (2026-01-28)
author: Priya Natarajan
customer_impact: p95 latency increased from ~680ms to ~1.9s for chat workloads. Approximately 4% of streaming responses experienced stalls >5s. No data loss.
summary: A change to the runtime memory watermark defaults caused aggressive KV-cache eviction under bursty workloads, leading to repeated recomputation and elevated latency.
timeline:
17:06 UTC: SLO alert for p95 latency on chat route fired (us-east).
17:10 UTC: On-call observed GPU memory oscillations and high cache evictions.
17:18 UTC: Identified runtime config change in 2026.01.28.1 setting low watermark from 0.85 to 0.70.
17:24 UTC: Rolled back runtime config for affected pool; evictions decreased.
17:40 UTC: p95 latency returned to baseline; monitored for stability.
18:02 UTC: Incident resolved.
root_cause: The serving runtime’s KV-cache manager used the low watermark to trigger eviction. The new default (0.70) was tuned for long-context batch workloads but was applied globally, causing churn for short, bursty chat traffic.
detection: Latency SLO alerts and GPU memory telemetry dashboards.
mitigation: Rolled back runtime config and pinned chat pools to the previous watermark settings. Disabled the automated config propagation job until validation was added.
what_went_well: Clear dashboards made the symptom obvious. Rollback procedure was well documented.
what_went_wrong: No workload-specific validation for memory watermark changes; config was promoted without canary on representative chat traffic.
follow_ups: Add perf-canary scenario for chat-bursty workload that fails on elevated KV-cache evictions (Serving Runtime; due 2026-02-20).
Split runtime watermark defaults by pool type (chat vs batch) and document in standards (Serving Runtime; due 2026-03-01).
Add change-management checklist item for runtime config promotions impacting memory behavior (SRE; due 2026-02-15).
